snippet.textDisplay: People often don’t realize what children go through when caring for their parents who need this level of care. I helped my parent, who didn’t have dementia, while also working full-time. While it made a big difference for my parent, it took a toll on me. I eventually had to step back because I was neglecting myself—so focused on caregiving that I wasn’t even eating properly and under a great deal of stress while doing so. So thankful that God kept me from having a stroke while caring for my parent.  🙌🙌🙌

Amen! It's better for the person with dementia too. There are more activities available to engage them with. There are a variety of caregivers for them to communicate with. They have others in their own age group to attempt at bonding with. If they can tolerate day trips, wonderful. If not, the activities and the entertainment comes to them in their controlled environment. You just have to do the homework of finding The Right Place! Miss Norma appears to be comfortable where she is.♡
This is hard work, the Memory Care facility can be a blessing for both parent and child. It's hard losing your mother to Dementia, mentally and physically. You're doing a fabulous job Crystal.

snippet.textDisplay: My mom had dementia and was very unpredictable.  I was her primary caregiver for six years. She died on July 3,2025. I miss my mom, but I don’t miss taking care of a childlike person who got younger as days went by. I survived the physical and verbal abuse. She died because her lung cancer came back for 3rd time and tumor in the brain that starting bleeding. Many days, I felt that i would die taking care of her, but God. Lord, I thank you for the privilege and honor to serve her. God gave us 5  extra years with her because I stop buying cigarettes for her. I thank God for his Grace and Mercy because she didn't suffer and died in peace in our home. It was my assignment, and it is not for everyone.  Dementia brings out stuff that the parent or children don't know about.

snippet.textDisplay: This is all very true and if you have never lived with a parent with dementia you just wouldn't understand. It is chaotic and draining. My mother was 90 years old and running away from her big beautiful home and climbing over fences to get out of her yard at her home that she didn't even know was her home. She has pulled knives on my siblings and we have had to call the police because we wouldn't let her leave the house at night in order to keep her safe while we knew my mother would never hurt her children as her normal self. You can do your very best but you are fighting a disease that is unpredictable. Memory care is not a lack of love but is a choice because you love and care for them. I'm thankful for the professionals who keep her safe 24/7.
